task: Allow a recoverable STALE release unit to re-enter the existing fresh successor reconciliation path after a previously blocking integration edge is repaired, without making BLOCKED or FAILED states auto-resumable or weakening exact-main, risk, scope, proof, CAS, or lifecycle authority.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Live bounded rehearsal run 37566854069 / job 112643423251 used trusted main 9453ef3270fd37ec85d4eb7b38793b713bcc105e and passed source fetch, trusted Knowledge/Atlas, Plan, Release Risk and reevaluation dependency bootstrap. The persisted active U01 remained STALE from the earlier fail-closed reevaluation attempt. The top-level driver accepts only PLANNED or PR_OPEN and threw RELEASE_UNIT_EXECUTION_STATE_UNSUPPORTED:STALE before fresh reevaluation could run. The core reconciliation function also currently rejects every non-PLANNED state, so merely widening driver dispatch would still fail.
observableOutcomes: A persisted STALE active unit is dispatched through prepareActiveUnit exactly like a unit needing fresh authorization, with current origin/main fetched first.
Core successor reconciliation accepts only PLANNED or STALE as entry states; BLOCKED, FAILED, READY, MATERIALIZED, PR_OPEN, VERIFIED, MERGED and CLOSED remain invalid reconciliation entry states.
A STALE unit can transition to READY only after the same fresh manifest, exact current-main lease, predecessor, risk, forbidden-scope, ordering and obligation-drift checks pass.
Successful authorization clears the previous blocker via the existing authorizeReleaseUnit transition rather than manual state mutation.
If fresh reevaluation or reconciliation blocks again, the unit remains fail-closed and the newly persisted blocker replaces the stale diagnostic through the existing event/state path.
unresolvedRisks: Over-broad resume support could accidentally make FAILED or policy-BLOCKED states retryable.
A STALE state caused by obligation drift rather than infrastructure incompleteness must not be silently converted to READY unless fresh reconciliation actually resolves all drift.
The driver and core state-machine eligibility must stay aligned so one layer cannot admit a state the other rejects.
Repeated retries must preserve CAS semantics and must not duplicate child PRs or bypass exact-head materialization checks.

in: Teach the release-unit driver to route active STALE units into the existing prepareActiveUnit path.
Force prepareActiveUnit to run fresh reevaluateSuccessorManifest whenever the active unit is STALE, even when order and target-base conditions would otherwise skip reevaluation.
Allow reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit to accept STALE as a recoverable reevaluation entry state while retaining every existing reconciliation proof and fail-closed check.
Add regression proof for STALE->READY after valid fresh reconciliation, mandatory reevaluation on same-base STALE, and rejection of BLOCKED/FAILED resume.
Add production-surface regression proof that the driver dispatches PLANNED or STALE to prepareActiveUnit and does not manually clear blocker/state.
out: No manual persisted state edit or blocker clearing.
No auto-resume for BLOCKED or FAILED units.

No changes to reevaluation dependency bootstrap, materialization identity, PR creation, merge authority, parent closure, Release Risk, Atlas, storefront, database, deployment, authentication, Builder or templates.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is a trusted release state-machine transition. A too-wide eligibility change could resurrect failed or policy-blocked release units, so the repair must explicitly constrain resumability to STALE and prove all existing fresh reconciliation obligations remain authoritative.

acceptanceCriteria: Driver invokes prepareActiveUnit for active state PLANNED or STALE and still fetches current origin/main immediately before preparation.
prepareActiveUnit invokes fresh reevaluateSuccessorManifest whenever active.state is STALE, including order-1 same-base retries.
Core reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit accepts PLANNED and STALE only.
Valid fresh reconciliation from STALE produces READY with blocker cleared and refreshed manifest/transaction identity.
BLOCKED and FAILED remain rejected with RELEASE_UNIT_RECONCILIATION_STATE_INVALID or driver unsupported-state behavior.
A repeated fresh reevaluation BLOCK from STALE remains persisted fail-closed; no PR is created.
Exact-head CI passes all canonical guards, Completion Truth verifies, Lifecycle closes, fix merges, then the unchanged rehearsal resumes from persisted CAS state.
invariants: STALE is recoverable only through full fresh semantic reevaluation, never by direct state reset or same-base shortcut.
BLOCKED and FAILED are not automatic retry states.
Current-main lease, predecessor receipts, risk, forbidden scope, ordering and obligation-drift checks remain unchanged.
Existing CAS persistence is the only authoritative state write path.
Child materialization/PR identity and parent lifecycle rules remain unchanged.

failureModes: Persisted STALE unit cannot be dispatched by driver.
Driver admits STALE but core reconciliation still rejects it.
Eligibility widens accidentally to FAILED or BLOCKED.
Fresh manifest still contains base, risk, scope, predecessor or obligation drift.
Concurrent executor attempt advances state and CAS rejects the stale writer.
edgeCases: U01 is STALE before any accepted materialization/PR state is persisted.
A later successor is STALE after a predecessor merge.
STALE reevaluation passes but materialization is already present remotely and exact reuse path is required.
STALE reevaluation blocks again with a different diagnostic.
Unit is BLOCKED or FAILED and must not enter resume path.

alternatives.summary: Treat STALE as the only additional recoverable entry state and rerun the complete existing fresh reconciliation path.
alternatives.reason: Preserves fail-closed authority while making an intentionally recoverable state actually resumable.

alternatives.summary: Rewrite persisted STALE units back to PLANNED before rerun.
alternatives.reason: Would mutate authoritative history and erase the blocker rather than proving recovery.

alternatives.summary: Route any non-closed unit back through preparation.
alternatives.reason: Would make BLOCKED/FAILED and partially executed states dangerously auto-resumable.

alternatives.summary: Introduce a second state transition/event solely for STALE recovery.
alternatives.reason: The existing AUTHORIZE transition already clears blocker and refreshes identity after valid reconciliation; a parallel authority is unnecessary.

specialistReviews.finding: The missing edge is dispatch/state eligibility between persisted STALE and the existing fresh reconciliation path.
specialistReviews.resolution: Align driver and core eligibility on exactly PLANNED|STALE and reuse existing authorization/event semantics.

specialistReviews.finding: Broad retry semantics could resurrect FAILED or policy-BLOCKED units and bypass operator/release authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: Whitelist STALE only and add negative regression proof for BLOCKED and FAILED.

specialistReviews.finding: STALE represents stale/reconcilable evidence, so recovery must recompute current-main authorization rather than restore old authorization.
specialistReviews.resolution: Fetch current main and execute prepareActiveUnit/reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit unchanged apart from STALE eligibility.

specialistReviews.finding: The live rehearsal proved two repaired edges can still leave authoritative STALE state that the orchestration loop cannot consume.
specialistReviews.resolution: Record #1004 and lock the exact resume state matrix with regression tests before replaying the persisted transaction.

challenge.scenario: A previous executor attempt persisted STALE because semantic reevaluation lacked a dependency; the dependency defect is later repaired but the state branch is intentionally left untouched.
challenge.finding: The driver currently exits before recomputing fresh evidence, making a fail-closed recoverable state permanently terminal.
challenge.resolution: Dispatch STALE into prepareActiveUnit, which recomputes the candidate against current main before any authorization.

challenge.scenario: A unit is FAILED because an accepted execution step violated an invariant rather than because evidence became stale.
challenge.finding: Treating FAILED as retryable could discard a terminal integrity failure and create a second execution history.
challenge.resolution: Keep FAILED outside both driver resume eligibility and reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit accepted states; prove rejection in tests.

challenge.scenario: A unit is BLOCKED by canonical risk/scope/predecessor policy.
challenge.finding: Blind retry semantics could turn an explicit policy denial into repeated execution attempts.
challenge.resolution: Keep BLOCKED non-resumable automatically; only STALE may enter fresh reconciliation.

challenge.scenario: A STALE order-1 unit is retried while its targetBaseSha already equals current main, for example after a transient reevaluation service or dependency failure that did not require a repository commit.
challenge.finding: If prepareActiveUnit reevaluates only successors or base drift, the old manifest could flow directly into AUTHORIZE and the prior semantic failure would be bypassed despite the state still being STALE.
challenge.resolution: Make active.state==='STALE' an independent mandatory reevaluation condition in prepareActiveUnit before any AUTHORIZE call; reuse the existing reevaluation result and fail closed again if it is not PASS.

challenge.scenario: Two executor attempts resume the same STALE state concurrently.
challenge.finding: Both may compute valid next state, but only one may authoritatively persist it.
challenge.resolution: Leave expectedStateCommit force-with-lease CAS unchanged; stale writer rejection remains mandatory.

challenge.scenario: STALE recovery finds an exact existing remote materialization from an earlier attempt.
challenge.finding: Creating a replacement commit or duplicate PR would break idempotency.
challenge.resolution: After successful fresh authorization, continue through the existing exact materialization reconciliation/reuse logic without special-case bypass.

challenge.scenario: A future refactor updates driver eligibility but not core reconciliation eligibility.
challenge.finding: The same unsupported-state failure would reappear one layer deeper.
challenge.resolution: Regression-test both the driver dispatch contract and core PLANNED|STALE state matrix.

challenge.scenario: Fresh reevaluation of STALE fails again after the repair.
challenge.finding: A resume feature must not assume retry success or clear the prior blocker prematurely.
challenge.resolution: Return/persist the newly produced fail-closed STALE blocker through the existing synchronize/persist path and create no child PR.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only and require Plan Before Code PASS before state-machine implementation.
Implement the minimal driver, prepareActiveUnit and core reconciliation eligibility changes plus positive/negative/same-base regression tests.
Require exact-head Knowledge, Plan, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Release Risk, full tests, typecheck, build and Completion Truth PASS.
Commit only canonical lifecycle closure metadata and require final exact-head CI PASS.
Merge the exact fix head, verify fresh main CI, then rerun the unchanged rehearsal from persisted STALE CAS state and accept only canonical U01 progression.

requirements.requirement: Trusted release-unit execution must be able to recover a persisted STALE unit only by re-running the complete fresh successor reconciliation path, while keeping BLOCKED and FAILED states non-resumable.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: STALE may not be cleared or converted to READY without full fresh reconciliation.
FAILED or BLOCKED units may not enter automatic resume dispatch.
